policy_basis: strictest_standard_wins — ABA + State Bar superset applied

R-LEG-001.name: Client Confidentiality Protection
R-LEG-001.description: All client information in documents must be treated as confidential. No client-identifying information may be exposed to unauthorized parties or cross-contaminated with other clients' data.

R-LEG-002.name: Client File Retention
R-LEG-002.description: Client-related documents must be retained per the strictest applicable state bar requirement (typically 5-7 years post-representation). Do not purge without verifying no pending obligations.

R-LEG-003.name: Privileged Communications Safeguard
R-LEG-003.description: Attorney-client privileged communications must be identified and given heightened protection — no AI-based analysis or external transmission without explicit attorney approval.
R-LEG-003.citation: ABA Model Rule 1.6, applicable privilege law

R-LEG-004.name: IOLTA / Financial Data Isolation
R-LEG-004.description: Documents containing IOLTA account numbers or client financial data per GLBA must be encrypted and isolated from general processing.

R-LEG-005.name: Encryption — Legal Documents
R-LEG-005.description: All legal documents containing client-identifying information must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). State bar requirements may be stricter.

R-LEG-006.name: Cloud Storage Compliance
R-LEG-006.description: Legal documents stored in cloud or shared infrastructure must comply with the strictest state bar cloud storage opinion. Vendor due diligence required.
R-LEG-006.citation: ABA Formal Opinion 477R, state bar opinions

R-LEG-007.name: Cross-Client Ethical Wall
R-LEG-007.description: When processing documents from multiple clients, enforce data segregation. No cross-contamination of client metadata, vectors, or document links.
R-LEG-007.citation: ABA Model Rule 1.6, Conflict of Interest rules
